tickets.subject: AR-900 losing IPv6 addresses on access VLAN after RA filtering
tickets.description: IronGate Freight NOC opened this after several warehouse scanners on the access VLAN began dropping IPv6 connectivity during a maintenance window. The affected device is an Aurora AR-900 running 9.2.3, and the router still shows the delegated prefix in configuration while clients lose their global IPv6 address roughly 3 minutes after the last upstream advertisement is filtered. TAC reviewed the event log and found repeated '%IPV6-4-RA-LIFETIME' messages at the time the clients stopped renewing their addresses. Initial checks showed the prefix valid lifetime was configured for 7200 seconds, so the observed behavior did not match the configured timer.
tickets.resolution: TAC identified this as KB-2104, where RA suppression on the active user VLAN causes SLAAC prefix state to age out on the 3-minute hold timer rather than the configured lifetime. We advised the customer not to suppress router advertisements on the production VLAN and to move the segment to DHCPv6 stateful addressing if suppression must remain in place. The team applied the documented workaround and confirmed new hosts retained IPv6 connectivity after the change.

tickets.subject: IPv6 clients dropping off after RA suppression on AR-900
tickets.description: HarborPoint Retail escalated on behalf of the customer after point-of-sale terminals on an Aurora AR-900 running 9.2.0 began failing new TCP sessions over IPv6. The loss starts about 180 seconds after the last valid router advertisement is blocked, even though the VLAN is configured with a 7200-second valid lifetime and the prefix remains present on the router. TAC saw '%IPV6-4-RA-LIFETIME' in the system log during the outage window, which aligned with the time clients lost their global address and Neighbor Discovery started failing. This points away from a pure host issue and toward router-side prefix aging behavior.
tickets.resolution: TAC tied the symptoms to KB-2104 and confirmed the router was removing SLAAC prefix state too early when RA suppression was active. We implemented the workaround by avoiding RA suppression on the active user VLAN and, where suppression is required, using DHCPv6 stateful addressing for the segment. After the change, the customer verified IPv6 addresses stayed valid past the preferred-lifetime transition and sessions no longer dropped.

tickets.subject: AR-900 9.3.0 SLAAC prefix expires early when upstream RA is blocked
tickets.description: IronGate Freight reported that an Aurora AR-900 on 9.3.0 was still advertising the prefix in configuration, but client devices on VLAN 10 lost IPv6 access shortly after a scheduled upstream filter change. The complaints were that laptops could still ping locally for a short time, then new connections stopped working and Neighbor Discovery lookups failed. No log extract was provided with the escalation, but the timing matched the typical 3-minute hold interval after the last valid router advertisement was suppressed. TAC confirmed the configured valid lifetime remained 7200 seconds and that the router itself had not removed the prefix from the running configuration.
tickets.resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-2104 and explained that this is a design constraint when SLAAC is combined with router advertisement suppression on Aurora AR-900. We advised the customer to stop suppressing router advertisements on the active user VLAN, or to use DHCPv6 stateful addressing for that subnet if suppression must remain. The workaround was applied and verified by the NOC, restoring stable IPv6 connectivity for the affected hosts.

tickets.subject: MetroLink IPv6 access loss on access VLAN during RA suppression
tickets.description: MetroLink Telecom emailed TAC about an Aurora AR-900 running 9.2.3 in a customer access site where IPv6 clients on VLAN 10 began failing after a change intended to reduce unsolicited advertisements from upstream. They reported that addresses disappeared from endpoints after about three minutes, even though the router still showed the delegated prefix and the configured lifetime was much longer. The log bundle included '%IPV6-4-RA-LIFETIME' messages matching the time of failure. TAC observed that the problem was limited to clients using SLAAC on the suppressed VLAN and was not reproduced on adjacent non-suppressed segments.
tickets.resolution: TAC matched the behavior to KB-2104 and confirmed the router was aging prefix state from received advertisements rather than from the locally configured timers while RA suppression was active. We instructed the customer to remove RA suppression from the production VLAN, or to migrate the affected segment to DHCPv6 stateful addressing if suppression must remain. After applying the workaround, the customer reported that IPv6 endpoints retained their addresses and new sessions completed normally.

tickets.subject: Northstar Bank AR-900 IPv6 sessions failing after maintenance RA filter
tickets.description: Northstar Bank opened a NOC escalation for an Aurora AR-900 running 9.2.3 after a maintenance change on the upstream edge caused IPv6 workstations in one office VLAN to lose connectivity. The bank reported that hosts kept their addresses for a short period, then new TCP sessions failed and Neighbor Discovery stopped resolving peers even though the router still displayed the delegated prefix. TAC found '%IPV6-4-RA-LIFETIME' in the logs during the interval when clients lost IPv6 reachability, which lined up with the reported 180-second delay after the last valid router advertisement was filtered. The configured valid lifetime on the prefix was 7200 seconds, so the observed expiry behavior was inconsistent with the intended network design.
tickets.resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-2104 and confirmed that the active VLAN was using SLAAC with router advertisement suppression, which causes prefix state to age out on the 3-minute hold timer. We applied the documented workaround by removing RA suppression from the user VLAN and recommending DHCPv6 stateful addressing if suppression is required for the site design. The bank validated that client IPv6 addresses remained stable after the change and closed the incident.
